question: The National Rice Research Institute is located at ________ in Odisha.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cuttack**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Rice Research Institute (NRRI) is located in **Cuttack, Odisha**.
 
• NRRI was established in the year 1946 and is one of the premier institutes under the **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR).**
 
• The institute focuses on rice research and development, and plays a crucial role in advancing rice cultivation techniques in India.
 
• NRRI also works towards addressing challenges related to rice production, such as pest management, yield improvement, and climate resilience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rice Research in India:**

 
 
• India is one of the largest producers of rice, and research plays a pivotal role in improving rice varieties and yields.
 
• Research institutes like NRRI contribute to the development of high-yielding and stress-tolerant rice varieties.
 
 
 
• **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR):**
 
 
• ICAR is an autonomous organization under the Department of Agricultural Research and Education, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India.
 
• It coordinates agricultural education and research in India and has numerous institutes dedicated to various aspects of agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Rice:**
 
 
• Rice is a staple food for a large portion of the global population, particularly in Asia.
 
• It is crucial for food security and provides essential nutrients and calories.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change and Rice Cultivation:**
 
 
• Climate change poses significant challenges to rice cultivation, including changes in rainfall patterns, temperature fluctuations, and increased frequency of extreme weather events.
 
• Research institutes like NRRI work on developing climate-resilient rice varieties to ensure sustainable production.
